description: The emulated machines the world runs, each named so a screen can show it; absent, no machine runs.

items.description: A named deterministic device whose lifetime is independent of its output consumers.

name.description: The instance identity used by displays, controls, and hardware operations.

configuration.description: The provider's versioned configuration, validated through its descriptor.
configuration.$comment: Open payload: this member's shape is decided by an id named elsewhere in the document, never by this generator.

running.description: Whether the host advances this instance. A stopped instance retains its hardware state.

memory.description: Ordered hardware bindings, independent of any display.

items.description: An ordered scalar binding between a named device and an Int world-state cell.

name.description: The binding identity within its machine.

direction.description: Whether values enter or leave world state.
direction.title: WorldMachineMemoryDirection

x-enumDescriptions.Read: Observe machine hardware and mirror accepted values into world state.
x-enumDescriptions.Write: Send world state into machine hardware.

format.description: The signed or unsigned scalar format: i8/u8, i16/u16, i32/u32, or i64/u64.

address.description: An unsigned raw address; mutually exclusive with Symbol.

symbol.description: An exported content symbol; mutually exclusive with Address.

key.description: The key of a table-shaped state row, or null for a slot.

access.description: inspect for reads; patch or bus for writes.

update.description: onChange or everyTick. Repeating a hardware-visible write requires explicit everyTick authoring.

conversion.description: checked by default; truncate explicitly admits narrowing and bit reinterpretation.

items.title: WorldMachineMemory

cable.description: The optional standing cable endpoint owned by this machine instance.

name.description: The cable's stable kebab-case name, shared by every plugged port.

position.description: This machine's 0-based place in cable order — contiguous across the cable's ports (validated), and what decides the linking engine's deterministic player order.

cable.title: WorldMachineCable

contentFolders.description: The folders holding the content this device can swap to, in the order they are listed and searched, each relative to the declaring document (WorldDocumentPaths), or null for a device with no swappable content. A folder that does not exist on this machine is listed as absent, never refused, so a world can name a local folder that only some machines hold. machine.content lists the files in them the device's engine can mount (WorldMachineContentFolder) and machine.swap mounts one by name; nothing outside the folders is listed. Omitted from the wire when null.

preferFolderDefault.description: Whether the device boots the default its ContentFolders name, when one names a file it can mount, in place of its configuration's authored content. A folder names its default in its own folder.json (SettingsFile), which the folder's owner writes (machine.default) and the boot and every world.reload read, so the default lives beside the content and no document names it. A device with no default set, or whose default is absent or unmountable, boots its authored content. Omitted from the wire when false.

runsWhen.description: The state condition the host advances this instance under, or null to advance it on every tick Running allows. The tick evaluates it against the arena after the rule frame folds and before the machines step (Server.WorldTick.GateMachines), so a rule's write starts or stops the machine on the tick it lands, and a replay or a restored checkpoint derives the same gate from the same state: the gate is never stored. A gated-off instance keeps its hardware state, as a stopped one does, and costs no emulation while it waits. It reuses StateCondition, the reading placement responses, binding overlays and portals share. Omitted from the wire when null.

contentBy.description: The state cell that selects which title of the machine's library it runs, or null for a machine whose content only its configuration, a folder default and operations decide. The library is the files of ContentFolders the engine can mount, in their listing order (TryTitle): the cell holding 0 runs the machine's own content, and n runs the library's n-th title. The tick reads the cell after the rule frame folds, beside RunsWhen (Server.WorldTick.GateMachines), and the host mounts a new selection on the tick it lands, so a rule that inserts a cartridge swaps the machine's content, a replay derives the same swaps from the same state, and no document mutation or provider operation is involved. The document always names the authored content (CaptureInstances reports it), so a title's name never enters the document, a capture or a tape. A selection naming no mountable title runs the machine's own content. Omitted from the wire when null.

state.description: The state row read; any declared numeric row (never Text).

key.description: The cell inside State, or null for its slot cell; refused when the row is keyed and this is absent, or unkeyed and this is present.

wrapFrom.description: The first title of the library's tail that a selection past the library's end folds into, or null for none: a selection n at or past it runs title WrapFrom + (n - WrapFrom) mod (count - WrapFrom + 1), so a title inside the tail runs as itself and any larger number lands on one. A world that does not know how many titles a local folder holds draws a large number (a seeded draw) and lets the library decide; a library with no title at or past it runs the machine's own content, as any unmatched selection does. Refused below 1.

contentBy.title: WorldMachineContentSelector

attention.description: How far the machine's attention reaches, or null for a machine the host advances on every tick Running and RunsWhen allow, attended or not. A machine that authors one is advanced only on the ticks it is attended (WorldMachineAttention) and is suspended on every other: its clock stops, it keeps its hardware state, and it resumes from that state on the tick it is attended again. The tick decides it beside RunsWhen (Server.WorldTick.GateMachines), from authority state alone, so a replay or a restored checkpoint derives the same ticks: the verdict is never stored. Omitted from the wire when null.

within.description: The distance in metres, finite and positive.

behind.description: How far behind a screen's face a body still attends it, in metres, finite and at least zero, or null for a machine attended from every side. A screen's face looks along its Right crossed with its Up (FixedFacing), and a body stands behind it by the distance from its position to the face's plane, so an allowance of about a body's height keeps a body beside or just behind the screen attending it. A screen a placement carries is attended by its holder whichever way it faces. Omitted from the wire when null.
